objections.claim_attacked: hypothesis + chosen_intervention + post_state: macro-loop cause named but not addressed
objections.objection: The hypothesis explicitly names a global-route path 'looping around the macro' as a separate suspected cause (tracked separately in #5971), yet the chosen_intervention only modifies layer adjustment and iteration count. The post_state claims GRT completion without resolving this named cause. If the macro-loop contributed materially to the 20k DRCs, the intervention is incomplete; if it did not, the hypothesis overstates its significance. The record does not settle whether this cause was material, creating an internal inconsistency between the multi-cause hypothesis and the single-cause intervention that claims resolution.

The record admits the exact meaning of the routing-layer-adjustment parameter is 'only explained in prose.' Without a mechanistic definition of what 0.45 versus 0.2 controls (e.g., cost multiplier, layer penalty, congestion threshold), the causal claim that reducing it from 0.45 to 0.2 resolves congestion is unverified. The record provides no technical basis for why this specific value change would fix 20k DRCs, nor does it establish the direction of effect (whether lower values make routing more or less aggressive).

mechanism_check: The causal chain is: high layer adjustment (0.45) causes routing to be 'too aggressive' and fail to converge; reducing it to 0.2 plus more iterations (35) allows GRT to complete. The chain breaks on two grounds: (1) the record does not define what the layer-adjustment parameter mechanistically controls, so the direction and magnitude of effect cannot be verified; (2) the hypothesis names a macro-loop cause (#5971) that the intervention does not address, making the claimed completion unexplained if that cause contributed materially to the 20k DRCs.
attribution_check: The direct_quote is properly attributed to eder-matheus (MEMBER) with date 2024-11-14 and locator. The quote supports the chosen_intervention's parameter values (0.45→0.2, iterations→35). However, the quote uses conditional language ('could finish GRT', 'complete BoomTile') while the post_state presents the outcome as achieved ('GRT was reported to complete'), creating a discrepancy between the evidence (a statement of possibility) and the claim (a statement of resolution).
missing_from_story: Mechanistic definition of the routing-layer-adjustment parameter (what 0.45 vs 0.2 actually controls and why lower values help)
Post-fix DRC count and congestion heatmap to demonstrate the 20k DRCs were actually resolved
Post-fix runtime to assess the cost of increasing iterations from 30 to 35
Whether the parameter change was actually merged as a code change (no PR link provided)
Resolution status of the macro-loop cause (#5971) and whether it was confirmed as a contributor
Explanation for why 0.24 placement density produced severe localized congestion at the top of the die and around the macro
